correctness.rationale: Exchangeable fixed-multiset sampling gives \(\mathbb P(D_i=1)=T/[n(n-1)]\). Adjacent-swap and reversed-word involutions yield \(c_i+c_{n-i}=p\). An explicit exhaustive ordered-three-copy count proves \(c_{i+1}-c_i=S/[n(n-1)(n-2)]\), including ties, giving the affine profile. Summation proves \(\operatorname{Cov}(M,I)=(3T+S)/12\); \(|S|\le(n-2)T\) gives the minimal size six and unique multiplicity profile \((5,1)\). Independent finite enumeration verifies 161 count vectors and 2,356 positionwise/scalar rational identities; this is corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem solves a natural complete finite-sample dependence question for jointly used inversion and descent measures in shuffled sequences with repeated values. It proves an affine all-position shape and at most one local sign change, and a sharp globally sign-reversing covariance that first occurs at size six, with a unique orientation/profile. These give motivated thresholds beyond routine isolated moment entries.
